results.controlIntent: Using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed system changes and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed system changes not approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved system changes are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Two CloudTrail events and the model registry entry reveal clear violations of CM-3(1) automated change control requirements:

**Violation 1 — Unapproved UpdateEndpoint (hotfix, 2026-03-15):**
Evidence item `b8f35f04` shows that `data-scientist-jdoe` executed an `UpdateEndpoint` call on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z deploying config `churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`. The evidence explicitly notes "no corresponding registry entry found." This means the change was made with no documented model package, no registry approval, and no approval workflow — directly violating sub-controls (a) document proposed changes, (b) notify approval authorities, (d) prohibit changes until approvals are received, and (e) document all changes to the system.

**Violation 2 — CreateEndpoint sequencing concern (2025-12-01):**
Evidence item `3ce695ab` shows the initial `CreateEndpoint` at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z. The registry entry (`4a5e70ce`) shows approval at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. While the timestamps suggest the deploy followed approval by 2 hours, the embedded evidence note explicitly flags this as a change-control sequencing failure. This warrants human review to reconcile.

**Overall:** At minimum, the March 2026 hotfix deployment represents an unambiguous, unapproved change to a production endpoint with no registry documentation — a direct failure of the automated change-control gate that CM-3(1) requires. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated approval-notification mechanism (e.g., SNS, EventBridge rules) that would satisfy CM-3(1)(b) and (f) — notification to approval authorities and completion notifications were not observable from available tools.

No evidence of a change-freeze or gate enforcement mechanism (e.g., IAM policy, SageMaker Projects pipeline) that would satisfy CM-3(1)(d) — the hotfix was deployed despite the absence of a registry entry, suggesting no hard technical gate exists.

The CreateEndpoint sequencing note in the CloudTrail evidence conflicts with the raw timestamps; human attestation or additional log evidence is needed to definitively resolve whether the initial deployment preceded or followed approval.
No registry entry exists for the hotfix model package version — a human reviewer should confirm whether an out-of-band approval process exists that was not captured in the registry.
